cards.english: We won't work tomorrow.
cards.existing: k → ğ between vowels. -ecek + -im becomes -eceğim, not -ecekim. Pronounced almost the same; spelling tracks the soft k.

cards.english: You don't read at home.
cards.existing: -iyor changes shape to match the root: gel-iyor, gör-üyor, kal-ıyor, bul-uyor. The suffix vowel echoes the root vowel.

cards.english: They aren't working at the library.
We aren't coming from the kitchen.
You read a poem usually.
We write a story usually.
You (formal) love homework sometimes.
We came home yesterday.
Could I see the menu, please?
cards.existing: `-malı/-meli` = 'must / should': `gitmeliyim` (I must go), `çalışmalısın` (you must work). Strong obligation; for softer 'should' use `gerekiyor` patterns.

cards.english: He/She is learning a song in the park.
We listen a story at the office.
Good morning, would you like some tea?
They sit/live happily.
I just arrived at school.
cards.existing: Past-tense person endings: -im (I), -in (you), nothing (he/she), -ik (we), -iniz (you pl), -ler (they). gel-di-m = I came.

cards.english: Good evening neighbor, how's it going?

cards.target: Biz geçen yıl markette alışveriş yaptık.
cards.english: We shopped at the market last year.
Hello friends, what are we doing today?
Good morning dear, would you like coffee?

cards.target: Bu yemeğin içinde et var mı?
cards.english: Is there meat in this food?
cards.existing: Question particle `mi/mı/mu/mü` floats – it goes after whatever you're asking about. `Geliyor mu?` (Is he coming?). Harmonizes with the last vowel.

cards.target: Marangoz güzel bir ahşap masa yaptı.
cards.english: The carpenter made a beautiful wooden table.

cards.target: Hem çalışıyorum hem de üniversiteye gidiyorum.
cards.english: I'm both working and going to university.

cards.target: Geçen hafta yeni bir araba satın aldık.
cards.english: Last week we bought a new car.
He doesn't go to the beach.
cards.existing: Turkish has no grammatical gender and no articles. `O` = he/she/it. `Ev` = a house OR the house (context decides which).

cards.english: You (formal) aren't going to school.
You aren't working at the beach.
They park their cars in the garage.
With the arrival of spring, nature comes alive.
She is a nurse at the city hospital.
You will arrive at the hotel soon.
cards.existing: Future = stem + -ecek/-acak + person. geleceğim (I will come), çalışacaksın (you will work). -ecek after front vowels, -acak after back.

cards.english: The firefighters are trying to put out the fire.
They will arrive at the restaurant in a moment.
He/She will arrive at the restaurant in a moment.
You will come to the restaurant in the future.
You walk in a serious manner.
The cat's fur sticks everywhere.
cards.existing: Three-noun chains work the same: `Ahmet'in arkadaşının evi` = 'Ahmet's friend's house'. Stack the genitives left-to-right, the final thing carries possessive.

cards.english: We've been reciting poetry lately.
The students' exams start next week.
Is there a cash machine nearby?
Take care, the weather is cold.
You are fond of poetry these days.
This weekend we will go on a picnic as a family.
cards.existing: Future tense uses `-ecek/-acak` + person ending. `gid-eceğ-iz` = we will go. The buffer `-y-` softens vowel clashes.

cards.english: Eighty percent of students passed the exam.
We left the beach this morning.
There are twenty-five students in our class.
cards.existing: Combined with the possessive: `arabam var` (I have a car – 'my-car there is'). Different structure than the locative form, both valid.

cards.english: The baker sells bread by the lake.
You (formal) saw at the market last year.
You took something from the kitchen last night.
You took something from the kitchen a moment ago.
cards.existing: Past tense = stem + di + person. geldim (I came), gördün (you saw), yedi (he ate). The di matches the stem vowel (di / dı / du / dü).

cards.english: They gave at the hotel a moment ago.
I will stay at the hotel next year.
Do you know what time the shop closes?
How much is this, what is the price?
The cats are wandering on the roof and sunbathing.
You came to the market a moment ago.
You found it at the hospital a moment ago.
He smiles to your face but talks behind your back.
I've been living in this city for a quarter of a century.

cards.target: Bu çantaları taşımama yardım eder misiniz?
cards.english: Could you help me carry these bags?

cards.target: Lütfen biraz daha yavaş konuşur musunuz?
cards.english: Could you please speak a little slower?

cards.target: Bu restoranda vejeteryan yemek var mı?
cards.english: Is there vegetarian food at this restaurant?
cards.existing: var = there is/are, yok = there isn't. No "to be" needed. Sınıfta üç kişi var = there are three people in the class.

cards.target: Komşumuzun kedisi bizim bahçeye giriyor sürekli.
cards.english: Our neighbor's cat keeps coming into our garden.

cards.target: Biz iki gün önce parkta başladık.
cards.english: We started in the park two days ago.

cards.target: Evimizin yakınında güzel bir park var.
cards.english: There is a beautiful park near our house.

cards.target: Biz iki gün önce havaalanına geldik.
cards.english: We arrived at the airport two days ago.

cards.target: Bir bardak su alabilir miyim, lütfen?
cards.english: Can I have a glass of water, please?
cards.existing: Negative ability: `gelemem` (I can't come – gel + e + me + m). The ability suffix wraps around the negation; word builds out from the root.

cards.target: Biletler ne kadar, indirim var mı?
cards.english: How much are tickets, is there a discount?

cards.target: Kedi pencerede oturuyor ve kuşları izliyor.
cards.english: The cat is sitting at the window and watching the birds.

cards.target: Geçen yaz ailece Antalya'ya tatile gittik.
cards.english: Last summer we went on vacation to Antalya as a family.

cards.target: Balıkçı her sabah göl kenarında sabırla balık tutuyor.
cards.english: The fisherman patiently fishes by the lake every morning.

cards.target: İyi akşamlar, bu akşam ne yapmak istersiniz?
cards.english: Good evening, what would you like to do tonight?

cards.target: Komşumuz öğleden sonra şarkı söyledi sonra dinlendi.
cards.english: Our neighbor sang in the afternoon and then rested.

cards.target: Dört katlı binanın en üst katında oturuyoruz.
cards.english: We live on the top floor of a four-story building.

cards.target: Müzisyen zurna ve darbuka sesinden çok hoşlanıyor.
cards.english: The musician really enjoys the sound of zurna and darbuka.

cards.target: Pilot uçağı kalkışa hazırlıyor ve kontrolleri yapıyor.
cards.english: The pilot is preparing the plane for takeoff and doing checks.

cards.target: Şu anda kitap okuyorum, biraz sonra gelirim.
cards.english: I'm reading a book right now, I'll come in a bit.

cards.target: Bodrumdaki eski sandıkta kehribar bir kolye vardı.
cards.english: There was an amber necklace in the old chest in the basement.

cards.target: Mektubu yazdım, zarfa koydum ve postaneye götürdüm.
cards.english: I wrote the letter, put it in an envelope, and took it to the post office.

cards.target: Deniz kenarında yaşlı insanlar bankta oturmuş sohbet ediyor.
cards.english: By the seaside elderly people sit on benches chatting.

cards.target: Günaydın komşu, bugün hava çok güzel değil mi?
cards.english: Good morning neighbor, the weather is really nice today, isn't it?
cards.existing: Yes/no questions use a separate particle: `mi / mı / mu / mü` (vowel harmony). It floats after the questioned word: `Geliyor musun?` (Are you coming?).

cards.target: Komşumuz her pazar pasta yapıyor ve bize getiriyor.
cards.english: Our neighbor bakes a cake every Sunday and brings it to us.

cards.target: Kedimiz her gün bahçede dolaşır ve kuşları izler.
cards.english: Our cat walks around the garden every day and watches the birds.

cards.target: Anneannem geçen hafta alışveriş merkezinde pahalı bir şemsiye gördü.
cards.english: My grandmother saw an expensive umbrella at the shopping mall last week.

cards.target: Bu kanyon hem derin hem de oldukça tehlikeli görünüyor.
cards.english: This canyon looks both deep and quite dangerous.

cards.target: Geçen ay İstanbul'a taşındık ve yeni bir hayata başladık.
cards.english: Last month we moved to Istanbul and started a new life.

cards.target: Okul ile ev arasında bir park var, oradan geçiyorum.
cards.english: There's a park between the school and home, I pass through there.
You (formal) go excitedly.
The tailor shortened my trousers.
We feed the cats on the street.
The captain is steering the ship toward the port.
The fountain in this square has been flowing for centuries.

cards.target: Ada kıyıdan birkaç kilometre açıkta görünüyor.
cards.english: The island is visible a few kilometers off the coast.

cards.target: Berber müşterinin saçını kesiyor ve şekil veriyor.
cards.english: The barber is cutting and styling the customer's hair.

cards.target: Bir orkide saksısı pencerenin kenarında zarif duruyordu.
cards.english: An orchid pot was standing elegantly on the windowsill.

cards.target: Bu yıl yağış miktarı yüzde otuz azalmış.
cards.english: The amount of rainfall decreased by thirty percent this year.

cards.target: Bu ağ ile şu şapka arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this net and that hat.

cards.target: Bu dere ile şu bordo arasında fark var.
cards.english: There is a difference between this stream and that maroon.
cards.existing: Combined with the possessive: `arabam var` (I have a car – 'my-car there is'). Different structure than the locative form, both valid.

cards.target: Bu zümrüt küpe ile şu safir yüzük arasında seçim yapamıyorum.
cards.english: I can't choose between this emerald earring and that sapphire ring.

cards.target: Bu makine işleri hızlandırıyor ama bazen sorun da çıkarıyor.
cards.english: This machine speeds up the work but sometimes causes problems too.
The movie was very moving, everyone cried.
The doctor will perform surgery tomorrow.
